A trajectory is not a special class — it is simply a [](`~mn.Molecule`) whose underlying
[](`MDAnalysis.Universe`) has more than one frame. Loading, styling and rendering all work
exactly as they do for a static structure. This page covers the extra behaviour that only
applies when there is more than one frame: playback, per-frame updates, and colouring by
values computed from a trajectory.

```{python}
#| warning: false
import molecularnodes as mn
import MDAnalysis as mda
from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD
from MDAnalysisData import datasets
from MDAnalysis import transformations
from MDAnalysis.analysis import rms, align
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import colormaps

canvas = mn.Canvas(mn.scene.Cycles(samples=16), (800, 800), transparent=True)
```

## Initial snapshot of the Universe

The simplest rendering is just loading the `Molecule`, adding a style and then rendering an
image — no different from a static structure.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-simple
#| fig-cap: A simple render of the atoms in the `mda.Universe`.
u = mda.Universe(PSF, DCD)
traj = mn.Molecule(u)
traj.add_style("spheres")
canvas.frame_view(traj)
canvas.snapshot()
```

## Playback

The connection to the `Universe` is maintained as the scene frame changes, so the positions
update live during playback. Several properties on the `Molecule` control how frames are
sampled and interpolated:

- [](`~mn.Molecule.frame`) — the current frame (synced with Blender's scene frame).
- [](`~mn.Molecule.subframes`) — interpolation steps inserted between frames.
- [](`~mn.Molecule.offset`) — a frame offset applied during playback.
- [](`~mn.Molecule.average`) — number of frames to average for smoothing.
- [](`~mn.Molecule.interpolate`) — enable position interpolation between frames.
- [](`~mn.Molecule.correct_periodic`) — apply periodic boundary corrections.

```{python}
traj.subframes = 2
traj.interpolate = True
```

## Selections from the trajectory

We can reset the node tree to clear existing styles, and selectively add them based on some
selection. The selection can be an `AtomGroup` or a string. If a string, first the existence
of a `Named Attribute` is checked and if it exists that is used as a boolean to apply the
selection. If the attribute doesn't exist, the string is used as an MDAnalysis selection
string — equivalent to doing `u.select_atoms()` and passing that atom group as a selection.

```{python}
#| label: fig-selections
#| fig-cap: Selectively apply the style using an MDAnalysis selection string.
median = np.median(traj.atoms.positions, axis=0)
# reset the tree to clear the previously added style
with traj.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    pass
(
    traj
    .add_style("spheres", selection=f"prop x > {median[0]}")
    .add_style("spheres", selection=f"prop x <= {median[0]}", material="MN Flat Outline")
)
canvas.frame_view(traj)
canvas.snapshot()
```

Transformations applied to the `Universe` (such as rotations or unwrapping) carry through to
the rendered molecule.

```{python}
#| warning: false
canvas.clear()

rot = [transformations.rotate.rotateby(90, direction=[0, 1, 0], point=np.zeros(3))]
u = mda.Universe(PSF, DCD, transformations=rot)

g2 = mn.Molecule(u).add_style("spheres")
canvas.frame_view(g2)
canvas.snapshot()
```

## Colouring by computed values

A common trajectory workflow is to compute a per-atom value with an MDAnalysis analysis and
use it to colour the render. Here we align the trajectory and compute the per-residue RMSF.

```{python}
adk = datasets.fetch_adk_equilibrium()
u = mda.Universe(adk.topology, adk.trajectory)

average = align.AverageStructure(u, u, select="protein and name CA", ref_frame=0).run()
ref = average.results.universe
aligner = align.AlignTraj(u, ref, select="protein and name CA", in_memory=True).run()

c_alphas = u.select_atoms("protein and name CA")
R = rms.RMSF(c_alphas).run()
u.add_TopologyAttr("tempfactors")
protein = u.select_atoms("protein")

for residue, r_value in zip(protein.residues, R.results.rmsf):
    residue.atoms.tempfactors = r_value
```

Compute a numpy array of color values `(Red, Green, Blue, Alpha)` that we can then store on
the mesh object inside of Blender that will be used for coloring in the final render.

```{python}
viridis = colormaps["inferno"]
col_array = u.atoms.tempfactors
col_array /= col_array.max()
col_array = viridis(col_array)
col_array
```

Create the `Molecule` object that will be visualised inside of Blender. After initialising
it, we store the computed colors as a `Named Attribute` on the mesh with the
`store_named_attribute()` function. These values can now be accessed in the rendering
pipeline.

To colour by our `Named Attribute` we build the node tree ourselves, reading the attribute
with a `SetColor` node before the style. In this example we render both as spheres and also
as a ribbon backbone — both of which use the colors we computed. The ribbon backbone takes
whatever color value is stored on the alpha carbon.

```{python}
# | label: fig-compute-color
# | fig-cap: "We can compute custom color values and then use those in the final render."
# | layout-ncol: 2
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "Spheres each use the atom's color."
# |   - "Ribbon and cartoon use the color from the alpha carbon."
from nodebpy.nodes.geometry import NamedAttribute

canvas.clear()
traj = mn.Molecule(u)
traj.store_named_attribute(col_array, "custom_color")

# NamedAttribute nodes must be created inside the tree-builder context
with traj.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    (
        atoms
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.SetColor(
            color=NamedAttribute("custom_color", data_type="FLOAT_COLOR")
        )
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.StyleSpheres(scale=0.8)
        >> join
    )
canvas.frame_view(traj)
canvas.snapshot()

with traj.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    (
        atoms
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.SetColor(
            color=NamedAttribute("custom_color", data_type="FLOAT_COLOR")
        )
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.StyleRibbon(quality=6, peptide_radius=1.5)
        >> join
    )
canvas.frame_view(traj)
canvas.snapshot()
```

## A sub-selection of atoms

When adding a style, we can ensure it is only applied to some selection of atoms. The
`selection` can be an `AtomGroup` or a string. In this case we pass an `AtomGroup` and the
selection is only applied to those atoms from the group.

```{python}
# | warning: false
canvas.clear()
adk = datasets.fetch_adk_equilibrium()
u = mda.Universe(adk.topology, adk.trajectory)
traj = mn.Molecule(u)
traj.add_style("spheres", selection=u.atoms[u.atoms.names == "CA"])
canvas.frame_view(traj.get_view())
canvas.snapshot()
```

## Streaming trajectories

A currently-running simulation can be streamed frame-by-frame rather than loaded from disk,
using MDAnalysis and IMDClient. See the [](`~mn.entities.StreamingTrajectory`) reference and
the [Streaming Trajectories](../tutorials/streaming-trajectories.qmd) tutorial for a full
walkthrough.
